Subject: Post-demo qualification & geo playbook

Hi Elaine —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Key takeaways from the call:
- Primary goal: reduce inference latency for short clinical prompts (<= 128 tokens) across US and EU while keeping cost per 1k tokens below your current hyperscaler baseline.
- Compliance: HealthAI needs EU data residency for EU customers and strong audit logs for PHI.
- Current infra: you’re mostly on hyperscaler managed endpoints (pay-as-you-go). Want a like-for-like perf/cost comparison and a migration playbook.

Proposed immediate next tests (attached test plan):
1) Multi-region latency sweep — run identical synthetic traffic from us-west, us-east, and eu-west and collect p50/p95/p99 for 128-token prompts.
2) Throughput/cost A/B — compare Dedicated Redwood pools vs your current hyperscaler endpoints for per-token cost and 95th percentile latency under sustained load.
3) Residency & ingress verification — confirm where data is stored and how logs/audit events are exported for EU traffic.

Attachments: redwood-geo-test-plan.pdf (test steps + required material), redwood-vs-hyperscaler-costs.csv (sample cost model)

Proposed timeline: kick off a 72hr pilot in each region next week (need your OK and a sample traffic generator / API token).

Next steps for Elaine/Max:
- Confirm which EU region you prefer for residency (eu-west-1 or eu-central-1)
- Share a short sample of representative prompts or a synthetic traffic generator (can be a zipped CSV).
- Any constraints on IP whitelisting or egress?

If that all looks good I’ll loop in Laura (infra) and Marissa (solutions) to propose the exact Dedicated pool configs.

Thanks —
Ben Carter

- EU region: we’d prefer eu-west-1 (Ireland) for now — aligns with our Ops controls.
- Data residency: for EU traffic we need the inference request and any stored logs to remain in-region; does Redwood Private/Dedicated support this?

Also, send along any expected delta in per-token pricing vs the hyperscaler — we need a ballpark before procurement greenlight.

Thanks for the context, Ben. Drafting a concise technical plan below — happy to iterate with Marissa and Elaine/Max.

Summary (short):
- Test window: 72 hours in each region; start target: 2026-11-09 00:00 UTC.
- Regions: us-west-2 (N. California), us-east-1 (N. Virginia), eu-west-1 (Ireland) — per customer request.
- Model: open 7B-family baseline (FP16) vs quantized int8 (via our quantization profile Q8_2). Run both variants back-to-back in each region.
- Dedicated config per region (minimal): 2xA10G GPUs per pool (predictable throughput for 100–500 RPS). If they push sustained >300 RPS we recommend 4xA10G.

Metrics to collect:
- p50 / p95 / p99 latency for 128-token prompts (client-provided sample)
- tokens-per-second and cost-per-1k tokens (from our billing engine)
- error rate and top error classes (timeouts, OOMs)
- KV cache hit ratio for repeated prefixes

Test execution notes:
- Warm-up: 10-minute ramp + 30-minute warm-up with cache prefill using a small subset of prompts.
- Load phases: steady-state at 100 RPS for 24h; spike test iterating to 500 RPS for 1h every 12h; end with a 6h longtail low-rate pass to observe recovery.
- A/B routing: we’ll provide an SDK-side routing stub they can drop into their generator to split traffic. We’ll run Redwood Dedicated vs their current hyperscaler endpoints 50/50 for all phases.
- Data residency / logs: configure ingestion endpoints for EU that write audit logs only to eu-west-1 S3 buckets under the customer-managed KMS. We’ll export a sample audit bundle daily for their compliance review.

Expected outcomes & acceptance criteria:
- p99 target: <= 250ms for <=128-token prompts in us-west/us-east; <= 300ms in eu-west (first pass).
- Cost: aim to be within +/- 10% of hyperscaler per-token cost on FP16; quantized int8 should show >= 20% cost improvement in most cases.

Dependencies from HealthAI:
- API token for the pilot (scoped) + IP allowlist if they enforce.
- Sample prompt CSV (10k anonymized prompts) and their k6 script.
- Decision on whether they want private control-plane (Private) or Redwood Dedicated with customer-managed KMS for logs.

Compliance items to prep for Procurement:
- SOC 2 Type II report (we’ll share our latest) — Ben, please surface to Elaine.
- Details on audit log retention and redaction options (we can redact PII and provide hashing options).

Next actions (owner):
- Ben: confirm pilot start window with HealthAI and collect sample prompts / token.
- Marissa: prepare customer-facing one-pager and procurement FAQ.
- Laura: provision Dedicated pools and prepare dashboards (latency/cost) to share daily.

If this looks good I’ll prepare an infra runbook and a short command list for the HealthAI ops team to ease onboarding.
